about.title: Early warning for peatland fires in Sumatra and Kalimantan
about.lede: ASAPify reads Himawari-9 and GK2A every 15 minutes over 65 peat regions: two geostationary satellites that look at the same peat from different angles, each the other's backup under cloud. Their thermal anomaly sets the status, measured against how dry the air is compared with its NASA POWER normal; VIIRS and NASA POWER only add support. On Alert an AI agent checks NASA FIRMS fire hotspots and NASA GIBS satellite images, and an operator decides whether subscribers in that province are told.
about.scope: Coverage: peat in 11 provinces of Sumatra and Kalimantan, as 65 NASA POWER grid cells (0.5° × 0.625°) that each hold at least 25 km² of mapped peat. Every satellite pixel in a cell is scored and the ones on peat are marked. A slot reaches ASAPify 20–30 minutes after the satellites scan it.
about.name: The name comes from asap, Indonesian for smoke.
about.step1_d: Himawari-9 (140.7° E) and GK2A (128.2° E) brightness temperatures at 3.9 and 10.4 µm, 2 km pixels, from NOAA's open data. Cloud is read from the 10.4 µm channel itself.
about.step2_d: ΔBT = 3.9 µm − 10.4 µm, against the clear pixels of the same cell, slot and satellite. A pixel is fire-like only if the 3.9 µm channel itself also rose: thin cloud raises ΔBT without it.
about.step3_d: ΔT is the mean of the satellites that see the region, weighted by how much each sees clear. Trapezoid memberships of ΔT give Safe, Warning and Alert; air drier than its NASA POWER normal moves the curves down by up to 1 K, and the midday sun moves them up by up to 1 K. VIIRS and POWER near the hotspot can only raise Alert. Cloud over 60 % means Not observable. Every change of status is recorded.
about.step4_d: On entering Alert, or when an operator asks, a Gemini agent built with Google ADK calls fetch_firms_data for VIIRS hotspots, looks at NASA GIBS true- and false-colour images of the region with the weather at the hot pixel, and answers Confirmed, Rejected or Needs manual review in YAML. The backend checks its numbers against what the tool returned, and sends a Confirmed to manual review when clear images from the last 24 hours show neither smoke nor a burn scar.
about.step5_d: The operator publishes or rejects each verification. The ASAPify bot posts every published alert in the ASAPify Telegram group; anyone can join it from Get alerts.
about.ai_rule: The status comes only from the data and the rules. The AI agent reads evidence for the operator and cannot change a status.
about.st_warning: Medium anomaly: ΔT counted about 2–7 K. Closer monitoring; no agent call.
about.st_noobs: Cloud over more than 60 % of the cell in both views, or no satellite data. Never counted as safe.
about.st_safe: ΔT counted below about 2 K: no fire-like anomaly in the satellites that see the region.
about.limit1: A 2–4 km geostationary pixel sees larger fires; small or smouldering ones often stay below its detection limit, where VIIRS (375 m) still sees them.
about.limit2: Clouds hide the ground from both satellites; such regions are Not observable, never Safe.
about.limit3: In daylight the 3.9 µm channel also sees reflected sunlight, so the thresholds rise by up to 1 K at midday.
about.limit4: A FIRMS hotspot is a thermal detection, not proof of fire. The images come from the last daytime VIIRS pass, often hours before a night observation, and cloud or haze can hide the place: an image never confirms a fire on its own.
about.limit5: The peat map in use (KHG) is incomplete, so a fire anywhere in the cell counts, marked on or off mapped peat.
about.data_note: All processing runs on Google Cloud: Cloud Run, Cloud Scheduler, Firestore, Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform (Gemini) and the Agent Development Kit.
about.src_himawari: Bands 7 and 13 (3.9 and 10.4 µm), 2 km, every 10 minutes; JMA, via NOAA Open Data on AWS
about.src_gk2a: Channels SW038 and IR105 (3.8 and 10.5 µm), 2 km, every 10 minutes; KMA, via NOAA Open Data on AWS
about.src_power: Hourly skin temperature and humidity, 0.5° × 0.625°, about 2–3 days behind. Humidity against its own 2021–2025 normal sets the dry-air shift; skin temperature is support only
about.src_firms: NOAA-20 and NOAA-21 near-real-time hotspots, 375 m: support near a possible hotspot, and the agent's evidence
about.src_gibs: Daily VIIRS NOAA-20 true- and false-colour images with its thermal anomalies drawn on top: what the agent and the operator look at
about.src_khg: Indicative map of peat hydrological units, KLHK

about.st_alert: Strong anomaly: ΔT counted about 7 K or more, from whichever satellites see the region. Dry air lowers the bar and the midday sun raises it, by up to 1 K each. The agent checks FIRMS hotspots and satellite images.
about.rules_note: ΔT counted = measured ΔT + dry-air shift − sun shift. Each trapezoid rises over the first range and falls over the second. The numbers are starting values: one night (11 October 2026) was checked against VIIRS, which is not a calibration yet.

rg.stale: Not current: the latest slot is {age} old (normally under 1½ h). The statuses shown may be out of date.

rg.legend.gk2a: GK2A hot pixel (a ring around a dot: both satellites agree)
rg.legend.viirs: VIIRS detection within 10 km and 12 h of a hot pixel

rg.trimmed: Part of this slot's pixel detail was left out to keep the day archive small.

rg.lag_note: A slot reaches ASAPify 20–30 minutes after the satellites scan it, and one is rated every 15 minutes. Dry air and the sun move the thresholds by up to 1 K each. The status comes from the rules engine; the agent cannot change it.

rgt.aria: Status, temperature anomaly, humidity and cloud cover for {n} slots
rgt.caption: {range} · dashed: rule breakpoints · hatched: not observable · shaded: day
rgu.none: Not rated: the slot is not observable, so no utility was computed.
rgu.note: Utility = membership of the counted ΔT in each status. ΔT counted = measured ΔT + up to 1 K when the air is drier than its NASA POWER normal − up to 1 K for the midday sun. The highest wins; within 0.05 the more severe status wins. VIIRS and POWER support can only raise Alert, and only when the counted ΔT is already high. A utility is a match score, not a fire probability.
rgi.no_support: none: no possible hotspot, or no VIIRS / POWER signal near it

rgi.power: NASA POWER: skin temperature (support) and dryness
rgi.power_dry: dryness {z}σ against its normal, last {h} h
rgi.sources: Brightness temperatures from NOAA Open Data (Himawari-9: JMA, GK2A: KMA). Humidity is a weather-model estimate (Open-Meteo, CC BY 4.0).

flag.daytime: Daylight: the 3.9 µm channel also sees reflected sunlight
flag.dryness_fallback: NASA POWER is late: dryness from the Open-Meteo humidity against the POWER normal
